title: Implemented-factor onboarding and constrained planning
purpose: Satisfy REQ-QUIC-CRT-0235 through REQ-QUIC-CRT-0240 with additive contract versions, mechanism-derived proof candidates, honest family boundaries, and exhaustive explicit planning.
design_summary: The additive planning line preserves all earlier artifacts and introduces generic versioned contracts for two audited implemented axes. Oversized admission, batch formation, and buffer coalescing form a directed admission/composition chain. Queued burst remains a separate actor-turn correctness family. Three nonlegacy values receive candidate-only proof chains. The retained v1 cell-space document preserves the checkpoint record; v2 defines effective-cell counts as including baseline, separates nonlegacy treatment counts, and separates disjoint cell partitions from overlapping annotations. The 12-cell admission space and 2-cell burst space are explicit and exhaustive; unsupported multi-axis cells remain capability-blocked.
data_and_state_considerations: Runtime policy mechanics remain unchanged. Evidence-only correlation uses fixed value fields and bounded operation identities. Catalog lookup, hashing, materialization, projection, and proof assembly remain offline. Workload and host identity are provenance only.
edge_cases_and_constraints: Single-fragment and bounded-multi-fragment are context-dependent distinct values and must not collapse merely because both can use a one-fragment fallback.
Queued single-datagram is inactive when the legal budget is at most one or the queue drains after one emission.

Raw oversized fragments structurally select one batch write, so the same operation cannot be both oversized- and batch-distinct; this operation-local noncoactivation does not prove that the configured workload cell is structurally inactive.
No new multi-axis execution capability is introduced.
alternatives_considered: Mutate retained schemas in place; rejected because historical fixtures and evidence require stable version semantics.
Put all four send axes in one family; rejected because shared performance outcomes do not establish a direct mechanism relationship.
Build a covering-array generator; rejected because the reviewed spaces contain only 12 and 2 configured cells.
risks: Candidate evidence must not be confused with externally reviewed proof.
Context-dependent legacy behavior signatures require activation-aware equivalence.
Future packet-flush onboarding must correct the queued-work branch of its delay predicate.
open_questions: After external review, should the two new proof values be promoted before any family interaction capability is considered?
Should packet_flush_cadence and queued_send_burst_budget form the next reviewed two-axis family?
